weather.tip: Rain showers are already falling with more likely tonight — combine that with Ganesha immersion crowds on lake and procession routes, and it's worth carrying an umbrella and padding your travel time if you're headed out this evening.

around.headline: Fake cancer drugs and ICU injections supplied to 90+ Bengaluru hospitals, pharmacy owner arrested
around.summary: Police arrested a pharmacy owner accused of supplying counterfeit cancer medicines and ICU injections to more than 90 Bengaluru hospitals at a discount, per The Indian Express and Business Standard. If a family member is on such medication via a third-party supplier, ask the hospital to confirm the batch and manufacturer directly.

around.headline: BMTC to share real-time bus data with aggregators
around.summary: BMTC will share live bus location data with app aggregators, per Construction World, meaning more accurate bus-arrival times on apps like Google Maps going forward. Worth checking your usual bus app for live tracking once it rolls out.

around.headline: 30-40% of streetlights not working in Bengaluru's Central City Corporation limits
around.summary: A large share of streetlights are out in the Central City Corporation area and are due to be replaced with LEDs, per Public TV English. Poorly lit stretches are worth avoiding on foot or two-wheeler after dark until fixed.

around.headline: Karnataka CM: be prepared for water and power shortages amid drought
around.summary: CM D K Shivakumar asked residents to be "mentally prepared" for possible water and power shortages due to drought conditions, per The Times of India. Worth keeping some water stored and checking your area's supply schedule.

around.headline: Centre scraps charges on UPI transactions up to Rs 2,000 and RuPay debit cards
around.summary: The Centre has prohibited merchant charges on UPI transactions up to Rs 2,000 and on RuPay debit card payments, per Live Law. If a shop or app tries to add a fee on a small UPI payment, you can now point to this rule and decline it.

around.headline: Meta agrees to report child sexual abuse cases amid India crackdown
around.summary: Meta has agreed to report child sexual abuse material cases to Indian authorities as the government tightens enforcement, per NDTV. Parents can use platform reporting tools with more confidence that reports will now reach the police.

events.name: Ulsoor lake immersion of 1 lakh Ganesha idols
events.note: Bengaluru's rejuvenated Ulsoor lake is set to receive around 1 lakh Ganesha idols for immersion, per The Times of India — expect heavy crowds and traffic near the lake through the week.

events.name: Gauri-Ganesh immersion processions across Bengaluru
events.note: Immersion processions continue to draw huge crowds at temples and lakes, per Udayavani and Deccan Chronicle — expect slow-moving traffic and detours on procession routes this evening and over the coming days.

events.name: 1.84 lakh Ganesha idols already immersed citywide
events.note: Five city corporations reported 1.84 lakh idols immersed by Monday, per The Hindu, with the eco-friendly mobile-tanker immersion points (659 tankers, 42 fixed tanks) still active for anyone who hasn't immersed yet.

street_smart.title: You run a small shop or festival stall and a customer pays by UPI, then shows you a phone screen with a green "Payment Successful" tick and a transaction ID before hurrying off. Your phone hasn't buzzed with the usual payment confirmation SMS yet. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Evergreen rotation (UPI fake-payment-screenshot fraud) — timed to today's news that the Centre has scrapped charges on small UPI transactions and RuPay cards (Live Law), which is likely to push even more small daily payments onto UPI. This mechanism hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: The stall is busy, there's a queue behind this customer, and the screen they showed you looked genuine — logo, amount, and a tick mark all present.

choices.text: Don't hand over the goods yet. Wait for your own bank/UPI app's actual credit notification or check your account balance directly before confirming the sale.
choices.feedback: Correct. A screenshot is just an image — it proves nothing about whether money actually left the customer's account. Your own app's confirmation, not their screen, is the only real proof of payment.

choices.text: Accept the screenshot as proof since the amount and tick mark look correct, and let the customer go so the queue keeps moving.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Fake or edited "payment successful" screenshots (and doctored SMS) are a well-known small-vendor scam — by the time you check your account and find nothing credited, the customer is long gone.

choices.text: Ask the customer to also read out the last 4 digits of the transaction ID as extra proof, then let them go.
choices.feedback: Risky. A transaction ID can be faked or copied just as easily as the screenshot itself — it isn't independent proof, since it still comes from the same source you're trying to verify.

choices.text: Politely ask the customer to wait a minute while you check, but let them pay by cash instead if they seem impatient.
choices.feedback: Risky as a habit — switching to cash on the spot avoids this particular scam, but doesn't teach you to verify UPI payments, so you're still exposed the next time you accept a screenshot on faith.

takeaways: Never release goods based on a screenshot alone — always confirm the credit on your own banking/UPI app, or wait for the SMS/notification tied to your own account.
Enable sound notifications for UPI credits on your phone so you don't have to check manually for every sale during a busy rush.
If you do get scammed this way, note the UPI ID/phone number shown and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930 — acting fast improves the chance of the transaction being traced.

quiz.question: A Bengaluru pharmacy owner was arrested this week for supplying what to over 90 hospitals, per The Indian Express?
options: Counterfeit cancer drugs and ICU injections
quiz.why: For critical-care medication from any new or unfamiliar supplier, it's worth asking the hospital pharmacist to confirm the batch number and manufacturer before it's administered.

quiz.question: What did the Centre recently prohibit on UPI transactions up to Rs 2,000, per Live Law?
quiz.why: The same rule also covers RuPay debit card payments, so a small shop adding a 'convenience fee' on a low-value UPI or RuPay payment is no longer allowed to.

quiz.question: What is BMTC set to start sharing with app aggregators, per Construction World?
quiz.why: Live bus-location sharing is what lets apps like Google Maps show an accurate 'bus arriving in X minutes' instead of just a fixed timetable.

quiz.question: Which Indian city corporation area was reported to have 30-40% of its streetlights not working?
quiz.why: The civic body has said the non-functional lights will be replaced with LED fixtures, which typically also cut long-term power costs for street lighting.

quiz.question: In India's UPI system, what does the 'transaction ID' actually prove on its own?
options: That the payment was successfully credited
Nothing by itself — it must be verified against your own bank/UPI app
That the payer has sufficient bank balance
That the payment is fraud-protected by the bank
quiz.why: A transaction ID (and any screenshot showing one) can be copied or fabricated; the only reliable proof of payment is your own account showing the credit.
